prompts.pocketLetterpressBack:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the attached mobile website mockup to show the AFTER state of tapping "Turn card". The input is the exact accepted FRONT state of Pocket Letterpress. Produce ONE standalone mobile screenshot at exactly the same tall aspect ratio as the input (853 x 1844 rendered pixels, representing approximately 390 x 844 CSS pixels). Not a comparison, not a collage. No phone bezel, OS status bar, browser chrome or annotations.
Preserve the original page composition, warm ivory textured background, header LA monogram, SACRAMENTO, CA location, the exact card outer bounds and size, cotton-paper material, subtle ochre edges, gentle shadow, colors, typography family, and every lower control. The card has completed a 180-degree rotation around its vertical center axis and is now showing its BACK, settled flat and readable. DO NOT show mirrored text or an edge-on intermediate state. Show no portrait on the back.
Replace ONLY the contents of the cream card and the flip control label. On the reverse face, the SAME beautifully tactile cotton stock with small blind embossed LA at top right. At top left in small olive text "Luis Augusto"; below, elegant large dark-olive serif heading "Let's stay" on one line and "in touch." below. Below heading, four spacious tap rows printed directly on paper, separated by extremely delicate pressed horizontal rules:
"Email" with smaller "hello@luis.app" and an outward arrow.
"GitHub" with smaller "@luisaugusto" and an outward arrow.
"LinkedIn" with smaller "Connect with me" and an outward arrow.
"Writing" with smaller "Read on Substack" and an outward arrow.
All rows have at least 44 logical px touch height; readable 15-16px primary labels and 13-14px supporting text at phone size. Fit rows comfortably within same exact card bounds, no nested panels, no icons in boxes, no invented biography, credentials, sample articles, QR codes or dates. Add a tiny olive "luis.app" footer inside the bottom of the card if it fits naturally. Keep the layout clear and breathable, not crowded.
Change "Turn card" below the physical card to "Show front", using the same curved gold arrow and same control footprint. Keep the wide olive "Save my contact" button, black "Add to Apple Wallet" badge, GitHub/LinkedIn/Email row and bottom Writing link in their exact original positions and visual style. Only the physical card turns; the rest of the page stays still. Material realism should remain exceptionally beautiful, soft, tactile, and clean. This is a faithful state change to an existing mobile design, not a new design direction.
prompts.rosePocketLifted:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the attached Rose Pocket mobile webpage to show the AFTER state of tapping "Lift card". This is a faithful interaction state of the SAME design, not a new concept. One standalone phone-content screenshot, same 853 x 1844 pixel aspect ratio as the reference, approximately 390 x 844 CSS pixels. No device frame, no browser or OS chrome, no before/after collage, no motion arrows or explanatory annotations.
Preserve the exact soft blush page background and paper grain, top LA mark, SACRAMENTO, CA label, dusty rose folded sleeve with thumb notch, cream card, portrait of the real user, brown-plum ink and beautiful serif and sans typography. Preserve all the lower save/contact controls, their style and approximate positions.
The interaction has completed: the cream business card has been drawn OUT and FORWARD and is now resting IN FRONT OF the rose sleeve, showing its whole front face. This is not a card flip. The sleeve is now clearly BEHIND the cream card, with its rose side edges and lower edge still peeking around the cream card, small dark inner lip and fine folded seams. The front cream card must cover the sleeve front, including most of the sleeve's "hello." text. There must be NO rose strip in front of the cream card hiding its lower content. Use correct occlusion, believable physical stacking, cream card casting a subtle soft shadow onto the rose sleeve underneath. Card floats very slightly, not wildly tilted. No giant vertical slide that cuts off the name or portrait outside the viewport. Keep card top below header, the fully exposed card bottom above the "Put back" control. The object stage has same approximate top/bottom extent as original. Show a clean completed pose, not an intermediate animation.
The lifted card exposes the previously hidden lower third. Upper portion: same rounded-square portrait, centered "Luis Augusto" in elegant brown-plum serif, "Product & Growth" and "Engineering" beneath in readable sans. Upper identity can be compact enough to fit the full face gracefully, without reducing body text below 14px CSS size. Hidden section now revealed: a delicate embossed horizontal rule, followed by three well-spaced rows printed directly on the cream stock:
"GitHub" on left, small outward arrow on right;
"LinkedIn" on left, small outward arrow on right;
"Writing on Substack" on left, small outward arrow on right.
Use clear 16px labels, each row at least 44px high, fine lines between, no nested panels or buttons inside the card. No invented posts, biography or QR codes. "hello@luis.app" stays in its existing position below the return control outside the card.
Change only the original lift control to "Put back" with a downward arrow, same cream pill. Beneath it keep "hello@luis.app", wide dark-plum "Save my contact", modest black Add to Apple Wallet badge, and bottom GitHub / LinkedIn / Email row. All visible within the same mobile viewport. Soft fibers, subtle embossing, lovely material depth, accurate warm shadows and calm stationery mood. This image must make it immediately clear what new useful content the lift reveals while preserving the accepted visual identity.
